E.#: Noun plural '-n' (Diagnose -> Diagnosen, Frage -> Fragen). Alone among the five plural affixes it does **not** mark its base singular, but singular *or* plural. It is carried by two kinds of entry: a singular that forms its plural in '-n' (Diagnose -> Diagnosen), and a form that is already plural and only adds the dative '-n' (die Lehrer -> den Lehrern, die Befunde -> den Befunden). Against the igerman98 hunspell dictionary as an oracle, 995 of the 10295 recognized entries carrying it are of the second kind -- and for the '-er' and '-el' nouns the base form is genuinely both numbers at once (die Lehrer, der Lehrer), so no single answer is right. A set holding both says exactly that: an inflecting noun whose number this flag does not decide. It constrains nothing in an agreement check, which is the honest outcome, and it still tells the capitalization linter that a bare '-e' word is a real noun rather than a verb form. Split out of 'Y', which generated '-n' and '-en' for every entry that carried it and so put one non-word into the dictionary for nearly every noun it touched. Which of the two an entry takes is decided per entry by harper-core/src/language/german/scripts/split_german_plural_n.py against the unmunched igerman98 list. 'E' previously held the 'ver-' prefix, which no entry carried.

G.#: Verb present 2nd person -st (du lernst, du arbeitest). Mirrors hunspell de_DE SFX X. Moved off 'h', which is the compound-capability marker sitting on nearly every noun: with the affix there, every one of them also generated 'arzneist'.

H.#: Bare '-s' on a noun that is not thereby a plural: the genitive of a proper name (Oesterreichs Hauptstadt, Goethes Werke, Peters Buch) and the '-s' of names that simply end in one. Mirrors hunspell de_DE SFX S. Deliberately not 'b', which is the same surface rule but declares the result a plural noun and the base one too -- true for 'Autos', wrong for 'Oesterreichs'. 'H' previously held an uppercase compound marker with no interfix that no entry carried and that the compound checker never read -- it reads the lowercase 'h' -- see the collision table in README.md.

I.#: Compound word formation - noun + noun with 's' interfix

K.#: Feminine derivation '-in' (Movierung): Lehrer -> Lehrerin, Biologe -> Biologin, Arzt -> Aerztin is irregular and stays a separate entry. Mirrors the singular half of hunspell de_DE SFX F, including the interior-capital spelling German writes as LehrerIn. The plural is on 'L'. 'K' previously held an uppercase compound '-n' interfix that no entry carried and that the compound checker never read -- it reads the lowercase 'k' -- see the collision table in README.md.

L.#: Feminine plural '-innen', the plural of the 'K' derivation (Lehrerinnen, Biologinnen, and LehrerInnen). Mirrors the plural half of hunspell de_DE SFX F. Split from 'K' for the same reason '8' is split from '7': the plural forms need a plural reading of their own. 'L' previously held an uppercase compound '-en' interfix that no entry carried.

o.#: Compound word formation - noun + noun with 'es' interfix (lowercase alias)

s.#: Strong preterite personal endings on a preterite stem (zog -> zogst, zogt, zogen; hielt -> hieltest, hieltet). Mirrors hunspell de_DE SFX Z. Strong verbs ablaut, so the preterite stem cannot be derived from the infinitive: igerman98 lists 'zog' and 'schrieb' as headwords of their own and this flag inflects them. 's' was the last character free in both namespaces -- see the collision table in README.md.

O.#: Adjective declension -e (feminine/neuter nominative/accusative singular) Mirrors hunspell de_DE SFX A, syncope and all: an adjective in `-el` drops the `e` (akzeptabel -> akzeptable, dunkel -> dunkler), `-uer` contracts (teuer -> teure), and a base form already ending in `e` takes the short ending (böse -> böses). The single `.` rule this replaces built `akzeptabele` and `dunkele` and never built the forms German actually uses.

Q.#: Adjective declension -em (masculine/neuter dative singular) Mirrors hunspell de_DE SFX A, syncope and all: an adjective in `-el` drops the `e` (akzeptabel -> akzeptable, dunkel -> dunkler), `-uer` contracts (teuer -> teure), and a base form already ending in `e` takes the short ending (böse -> böses). The single `.` rule this replaces built `akzeptabele` and `dunkele` and never built the forms German actually uses.

R.#: Adjective declension -en (plural and masculine/neuter genitive singular) Mirrors hunspell de_DE SFX A, syncope and all: an adjective in `-el` drops the `e` (akzeptabel -> akzeptable, dunkel -> dunkler), `-uer` contracts (teuer -> teure), and a base form already ending in `e` takes the short ending (böse -> böses). The single `.` rule this replaces built `akzeptabele` and `dunkele` and never built the forms German actually uses.

S.#: Adjective declension -er (masculine nominative singular) Mirrors hunspell de_DE SFX A, syncope and all: an adjective in `-el` drops the `e` (akzeptabel -> akzeptable, dunkel -> dunkler), `-uer` contracts (teuer -> teure), and a base form already ending in `e` takes the short ending (böse -> böses). The single `.` rule this replaces built `akzeptabele` and `dunkele` and never built the forms German actually uses.

T.#: Adjective declension -es (neuter nominative/accusative singular) Mirrors hunspell de_DE SFX A, syncope and all: an adjective in `-el` drops the `e` (akzeptabel -> akzeptable, dunkel -> dunkler), `-uer` contracts (teuer -> teure), and a base form already ending in `e` takes the short ending (böse -> böses). The single `.` rule this replaces built `akzeptabele` and `dunkele` and never built the forms German actually uses.

U.#: Adjective comparative, declined (groß -> größere, teuer -> teurere). Mirrors hunspell de_DE SFX C.

W.#: Adjective superlative, declined (groß -> größte, komplex -> komplexesten). Mirrors hunspell de_DE SFX C.

X.#: Noun plural -e (Frau -> Frauen) A noun in `-nis` doubles the `s`: `Ergebnis` -> `Ergebnisse`, never `*Ergebnise`. The three remaining conditions are the complement of `nis`, spelled out because the affix matcher has no alternation: `[^s]` is everything not ending in `s`, `[^i]s` and `[^n]is` are the words that do end in `s` without being a `-nis` (`Kreise`, `Hauses`).

Y.#: Noun plural '-en' (Student -> Studenten, Aufklärung -> Aufklärungen). The '-n' half moved to 'E': carrying both put a non-word into the dictionary for nearly every noun, since a German noun takes one or the other. See harper-core/src/language/german/scripts/split_german_plural_n.py A noun in `-nis` doubles the `s`: `Ergebnis` -> `Ergebnissen`. See the note on `X` for why the complement of `nis` is spelled out in three conditions.

a.#: Noun plural -er, with the dative -ern (die Bilder, den Bildern). Mirrors hunspell de_DE SFX R. The umlauted stems are separate entries; the rule itself does not umlaut, which is why the old one-line version generated 'manner' for 'Mann'.

c.#: Verb present participle, declined (lern-end, lern-ende, lern-enden). Mirrors hunspell de_DE SFX D, which simply hangs `d`, `de`, `dem`, `den`, `der`, `des` on any word ending in `n`. Here it attaches to the stem like the other conjugation flags, so `-en` comes off first. Verbs in `-ern` and `-eln` are the exception and keep their `n`: the participle of `entwickeln` is `entwickelnd`, not `entwickelend`, and of `speichern` `speichernd`, not `speicherend`. Getting that wrong put the non-words in the dictionary and left the real forms out of it.

i.#: Verb present -t (lern-t). NOTE: like 'h', 'i' is also used as a bookkeeping marker on noun entries, so it must not inject a part of speech. It only generates the -t surface form; the verb reading comes from 'V'/'j'/'f'/'d'/'e'.

k.#: Verb past participle -t (regular verbs: ge-macht, ge-lernt)

l.#: Verb past participle -en (strong verbs: ge-schrieben, ge-laufen)

m.#: Verb past participle without ge- prefix (insep. prefixes: be-, er-, ver-, zer-, ent-, emp-)

n.#: Declined past participle (das automatisierte Verfahren, ein beobachteter Vorgang). Mirrors hunspell de_DE SFX O, and attaches to the verb stem like the other conjugation flags. Only the participles formed without `ge-` belong here -- the `-ieren` verbs and the inseparable prefixes -- which is what the oracle in harper-core/src/language/german/scripts/add_german_verb_derivations.py confirms per entry. `n` previously held a participle class whose one rule listed the separable prefixes as `(ab|an|auf|...)`; the affix matcher has no alternation, so that condition could never match, and no entry carried the flag.

z.#: '-chen' diminutive (das Körperchen, das Röhrchen, des Röhrchens). Mirrors hunspell de_DE SFX M, including the three stems that umlaut before the doubled s (Fass -> Fässchen, Schloss -> Schlösschen, Kuss -> Küsschen). A diminutive is always neuter, whatever the base noun is, which is why the class sets the gender. `z` previously held a neuter-noun property that duplicated `Z` and that no entry carried.

x.#: '-bar' derivation: the adjective that says the verb can be done to something (lesbar, beeinflussbar, bearbeitbare). Mirrors hunspell de_DE SFX B and attaches to the verb stem, so the infinitive ending comes off first. Not every transitive verb takes it -- there is no *gebbar* -- so the flag is set per entry by an oracle, see harper-core/src/language/german/scripts/add_german_verb_derivations.py. `x` previously held an imperative-mood property that no entry carried.

7.#: '-ung' nominalization of a verb. Mirrors hunspell de_DE SFX J: the suffix attaches to the verb stem, so the infinitive ending is stripped first (entscheiden -> Entscheidung, sammeln -> Sammlung, ändern -> Änderung). Pair with '8' for the plural.

8.#: '-ungen', the plural of the '7' nominalization. Mirrors hunspell de_DE SFX J: the suffix attaches to the verb stem, so the infinitive ending is stripped first (entscheiden -> Entscheidung, sammeln -> Sammlung, ändern -> Änderung). A separate flag because `target` metadata is per flag, not per replacement, and the plural has to be marked as one.

9.#: 'un-' negating prefix (unangenehm, unbekannt). Mirrors hunspell de_DE PFX U. Cross-product so the prefixed form still takes the base's declension suffixes: un + bekannt -> unbekannt -> unbekannte. A digit because affixes and properties share one namespace and 'U' is already the adjective comparative.

0.#: Noun genitive -es (des Hauses). Mirrors hunspell de_DE SFX T. Lives on a digit because the letter 'N' is also the *noun* property: with the affix there it reached every entry tagged a noun and generated 'ergebnises' and 'altertumes' for the great majority of them. A noun in `-nis` doubles the `s`: `Ergebnis` -> `Ergebnisses`. See the note on `X` for why the complement of `nis` is spelled out in three conditions.

1.#: Spelled-out cardinal numeral (German). Lower case in running text; used attributively it licenses a following noun.

2.#: Unit abbreviation (German), e.g. km, kg, kWh. Written lower case and must never be 'corrected' to a capitalized noun.

3.#: Latin/Greek etymology term appearing lower case in German prose (de facto, Homo sapiens). Not a miscapitalized German noun.

4.#: Determiner (German): articles and other determiners. Collision-free digit flag; the letter 'D' is also the -ung affix and would generate junk forms.

5.#: Pronoun (German). Collision-free digit flag; the letter 'I' is also the noun+s compound interfix affix.

6.#: Conjunction (German). Collision-free digit flag; the letter 'C' is also the -keit suffix affix.

A.#: Singular noun (German). For a noun whose plural this dictionary cannot generate -- Bruder/Brueder, Vater/Vaeter and the rest of the umlaut plurals -- so that it carries no plural flag and would otherwise have no number at all. Without it 'mit den Bruder' is invisible, because the dative plural reading of 'den' survives unchallenged. Not given to a noun whose singular and plural are spelled alike ('-er', '-el', '-en'), nor to a plurale tantum. 'A' previously held an unused alias of the adjective property 'J'; the flag namespace is full, so a new flag has to come from a retired one.

X.#: noun plural -e (German). This letter is an affix as well as a property and both fire, so the number is set by the affix on the form it builds and never here -- see 'A plural flag said the opposite of what it meant' in README.md.

E.#: noun plural -n (German) - the '-n' half of the old 'Y', see harper-core/src/language/german/scripts/split_german_plural_n.py. This letter is an affix as well as a property and both fire, so the number is set by the affix on the form it builds and never here -- see 'A plural flag said the opposite of what it meant' in README.md.

Y.#: noun plural -en (German). This letter is an affix as well as a property and both fire, so the number is set by the affix on the form it builds and never here -- see 'A plural flag said the opposite of what it meant' in README.md.

a.#: noun plural -er with umlaut (German). This letter is an affix as well as a property and both fire, so the number is set by the affix on the form it builds and never here -- see 'A plural flag said the opposite of what it meant' in README.md.

b.#: noun plural -s (German). This letter is an affix as well as a property and both fire, so the number is set by the affix on the form it builds and never here -- see 'A plural flag said the opposite of what it meant' in README.md.

g.#: verb past participle property (German: ge- prefix)

q.#: Compound adjective flag - words with this flag can participate in adjective compound formation

y.#: Subjunctive I mood flag (German - Konjunktiv I)

*.#: Stem-only marker. The entry is not a word: it exists so the conjugation affixes have something to attach to (`absperr/~~*Vcej` builds `absperrt`, `absperrte`, `absperren`). Without it the bare stem lands in the word list, is accepted as a spelling, and — because every list member may be a compound element — turns up inside misspellings such as `Absiecht` = `ab` + `siecht`. Hunspell calls this `NEEDAFFIX`.

h.#: Compound-capability marker. Generates nothing — it is bookkeeping, appended to nearly every vetted noun entry, and `CompoundChecker` reads it to decide whether a short word may act as a compound element. The '-st' affix that used to live here moved to 'G'.
